title: Grateful Dead Live at The Ark on 1969-04-22

ai_review.summary: Super‑69 soundboard captures a magical Boston Ark show highlighted by an epic Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star journey and tight performances of The Eleven and The Other One.
ai_review.review: The April‑22‑1969 Ark recording is praised for its pristine soundboard mix—despite minor tape hiss, early‑set mic feedback and a regrettable cut in The Other One—and for delivering one of the era’s most compelling Dark Stars, buoyed by soaring Jerry Garcia leads and a thunderous dual‑drum section. Reviewers repeatedly cite the seamless transition from Mountains of the Moon into Dark Star, the powerful Eleven, and strong early‑set material as show highlights.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly high reviewer scores (average ~4.55) and consistent praise for both performance and recording outweigh the few technical complaints, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, balanced mix praised as an "audio masterpiece" with excellent stereo drum placement; minor issues noted include tape hiss, early‑set mic feedback and a major splice loss in The Other One.

standout_songs: Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star
Sitting on Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: Set opens with a crisp Sitting on Top of the World, builds momentum through Mountains of the Moon into an expansive Dark Star, and maintains high energy with The Eleven and a strong second‑set sequence despite a missing segment in The Other One.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for raw energy, soaring guitar solos, powerful vocals, and his leadership on the long Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as “monster on the bass” during The Other One; strong interplay with Jerry throughout the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned mainly for occasional vocal contributions; no specific instrumental praise beyond that.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ is highlighted as prominent and well‑balanced in the mix, adding depth to the performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart receive special commendation for tight stereo placement, especially on The Eleven and overall rhythmic drive.
